---
title: "Columns"
---

The `column_spec` array defines one entry per column.

## Fields

| Field       | Type    | Required | Description                          |
|-------------|---------|----------|--------------------------------------|
| `id`        | string  | Yes      | Unique column identifier             |
| `align`     | string  | No (default `"left"`) | `"left"`, `"center"`, `"right"`, `"justify"`, or `"char"` |
| `align_char`| string? | No       | Character for char alignment (e.g. `"."`) |
| `width`     | string  | Yes      | `"auto"` or CSS length               |
| `min_width` | string? | No       | Minimum width                        |
| `max_width` | string? | No       | Maximum width                        |
| `style_id`  | string? | No       | Default style for all cells in column|
| `hidden`    | boolean | Yes      | Whether column is hidden             |
| `label`     | string? | No       | Column display label (accessibility) |

## Example

```json
{
  "column_spec": [
    { "id": "col_0", "align": "left", "width": "150px", "hidden": false, "label": "Country" },
    { "id": "col_1", "align": "right", "width": "auto", "hidden": false, "label": "Population" },
    { "id": "col_2", "align": "center", "width": "1fr", "hidden": false, "label": "Region" }
  ]
}
```

## Width Values

| Value   | Description                                    |
|---------|------------------------------------------------|
| `auto`  | Content-determined width                       |
| `120px` | Fixed pixel width                              |
| `25%`   | Share of the table's width                     |
| `1fr`   | Share of what the other columns leave          |
| `3cm`   | Absolute length (cm, mm, in, pt)               |

The table's width is `config.table_width` when set, else the width of the line
(the page's text width, or the container's). `fr` columns divide what the fixed and
`%` columns leave, in proportion to their numbers (`2fr` is twice `1fr`). When the
table has a width and no column is `fr`, the `auto` columns share what the others
leave, so the table is as wide as it says; a table whose columns all have fixed or
`%` widths is as wide as they add up to. HTML leaves the sizing to the browser; how
each other format sizes its columns is in [Output Formats](../guide/output-formats.qmd).

`min_width` and `max_width` take the same forms except `fr` and `auto`. Widths may not
be negative; an invalid width fails validation with `INVALID_LENGTH` (see
[Validation](validation.qmd#lengths)).
